problem_motivation.content: Understanding the behavior of high entropy alloys at finite temperature is hindered by incomplete experimental data for single-phase alloys.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Understanding their behavior at finite temperature is, however, limited by the incomplete experimental data for single-phase alloys.

problem_motivation.content: Understanding the magnetic properties of the Cantor alloy in both fcc and hcp phases remains very scarce.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: In contrast to the intensive investigations of the mechanical properties of the Cantor alloy, understanding the magnetic properties remains very scarce in both the fcc and hcp phases.

problem_motivation.content: There has been no attempt to explore the role of thermal longitudinal spin fluctuations (LSFs) in PM CoCrFeMnNi HEA despite its interest.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: However, to our best knowledge, there has been no attempt yet to explore the role of thermal LSFs in PM CoCrFeMnNi HEA for neither the fcc nor hcp phase, in spite of its high fundamental and practical interest.

prior_approach.content: Prior work has demonstrated the crucial role of LSFs in describing finite-temperature magnetic properties of other magnetic metals and alloys.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The crucial role of LSFs in the accurate description of finite-temperature magnetic properties has been demonstrated in a few magnetic metals including PM bcc (body-centered cubic) and fcc Fe, fcc Ni and fcc Co [30] – [34] , and in alloys such as PM fcc/hcp Fe-Mn and Fe-Cr-Ni systems [29] , [35] – [38] .

prior_approach.content: Reference to the thermodynamic model proposed by Olson and Cohen used to evaluate stacking fault energy.
prior_approach.evidence_span: the thermodynamic model proposed by Olson and Cohen [41] was formulated to evaluate γ isf

prior_approach.content: The LSF methodology from Dong et al. is adopted for describing the finite-temperature magnetic state.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The LSF methodology proposed by Dong et al . [29] , [30] was adopted to describe the finite-temperature magnetic state of each alloy species in PM CoCrFeMnNi HEA.

prior_approach.content: The Olson and Cohen thermodynamic model is utilized to compute stacking fault energy.
prior_approach.evidence_span: thermodynamic model proposed by Olson and Cohen [41] to compute the stacking fault energy γ isf .

prior_approach.content: The EMTO method is used as the framework for DFT calculations.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Kohn-Sham equations were solved within the framework of the exact muffin-tin orbitals (EMTO) method [45] – [48]

prior_approach.content: The DLM picture and CPA are adopted for describing magnetic and chemical disorders.
prior_approach.evidence_span: magnetic and chemical disorders were described by the DLM picture [26] – [28] in combination with the coherent-potential approximation (CPA) [50] , [51] .

prior_approach.content: The PBE parametrization is used for the generalized gradient approximation.
prior_approach.evidence_span: generalized gradient approximation as parametrized by Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE) [49]

prior_limitation.content: Accurate accounting of magnetic excitations at finite temperature remains a particular challenge due to the lack of a complete theory for itinerant electron magnetism.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: However, at finite temperature, a proper account of magnetic excitations, both transversal and longitudinal spin fluctuations (LSFs), is of particular challenge for magnetic transition metals and alloys like the Cantor alloy, owing to the lack of a complete theory for itinerant electron magnetism [24] , [25] .

prior_limitation.content: Previous studies have not applied LSF exploration to PM CoCrFeMnNi HEA for either fcc or hcp phases.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: However, to our best knowledge, there has been no attempt yet to explore the role of thermal LSFs in PM CoCrFeMnNi HEA for neither the fcc nor hcp phase

prior_limitation.content: Previous calculations in ref [42] report higher magnitudes of stacking fault energy because they do not account for the reduction of magnetic contribution due to LSFs.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: the magnitudes of γ isf accounting for LSFs are lower than those found in ref. [42] , because the magnetic contribution determined in the work is significantly reduced owing to LSFs.

causal_claim.content: The hcp phase being energetically preferable to the fcc phase at cryogenic temperatures leads to negative stacking fault energy.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The hcp phase is energetically preferable to the fcc one at cryogenic temperatures, which results in negative stacking fault energy at these conditions.

causal_claim.content: Increasing temperature causes the stacking fault energy to increase, which in turn suppresses the formation of stacking faults and nano-twins.
causal_claim.evidence_span: With increasing temperature, the stacking fault energy increases, suppressing the formation of stacking faults and nano-twins.

causal_claim.content: The reduced stacking fault energy at cryogenic temperatures enhances plastic deformation by nano-twins and stacking faults.
causal_claim.evidence_span: With decreasing temperature, the plastic deformation by nano-twins and stacking faults is enhanced owing to the reduced γ isf

mechanism_principle.content: The positive temperature dependence of stacking fault energy is ultimately dominated by magneto-volume coupling at thermal excitations.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The positive temperature dependence of γ isf is ultimately dominated by the magneto-volume coupling at thermal excitations.

mechanism_principle.content: The low stacking fault energy at cryogenic temperatures is attributed to the thermodynamic stability of the hcp phase relative to the fcc phase.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The low γ isf is attributed to the fact that the hcp phase is thermodynamically stable to the fcc one at these conditions

mechanism_principle.content: The role of LSFs in this alloy is consistent with findings in PM gamma-Fe and Fe-22.5 at.% Mn.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The role of LSFs disclosed in PM CoCrFeMnNi is in good agreement with that reported in PM γ -Fe [39] and Fe-22.5 at.% Mn [36] .

evidence_result.content: Measured mean magnetic moments for alloy components (Co, Cr, Fe, Mn, Ni) at various temperatures in fcc and hcp phases under LSFs and thermal expansion.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Table 1. The mean magnetic moments { m I } of alloy components in PM CoCrFeMnNi as a function of temperature for the fcc and hcp phases when considering the effect of LSFs in combination with thermal lattice expansion.

evidence_result.content: Critical temperature for fcc-hcp phase transition determined to be ~430 K in LSF calculations.
evidence_result.evidence_span: the critical temperature of fcc-hcp phase transition at ambient pressure is determined to be ~430 K in the LSF calculations

evidence_result.content: Stacking fault energy predicted to range from -17 mJ m-2 at 50 K to 31 mJ m-2 at 1000 K when accounting for LSFs and lattice expansion.
evidence_result.evidence_span: the γ isf of PM CoCrFeMnNi is predicted from the LSF calculations to increase from −17 mJ m −2 at 50 K, reach zero at ~260 K and keep rising to 31 mJ m −2 at 1000 K

evidence_result.content: Interfacial energy sigma estimated to vary between ~3.1 and 6.0 mJ m-2 for LSF calculations in the 50-1200 K range.
evidence_result.evidence_span: the σ of PM CoCrFeMnNi is estimated to slightly vary in the range of ~3.1–6.0 and 3.6–6.8 mJ m −2 for the LSF and FS calculations, respectively.

constraint.content: The calculation assumes an ideal c/a ratio of 8/3 for the hcp structure.
constraint.evidence_span: an ideal c / a ratio of 8/3 was employed for the hcp structure

constraint.content: The finite-temperature volume of the hcp structure is constrained to be identical to the fcc volume.
constraint.evidence_span: the finite-temperature volume of which was assumed to be identical with the fcc one.

constraint.content: Structural relaxation in the faulted supercell is omitted as a constraint of the setup.
constraint.evidence_span: The structural relaxation in the faulted supercell was omitted.
